 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

 Misc. Appeal No. 448 of 2021
 Gaytri Dikshit
 Versus
 The New India Insurance Company Ltd And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Abhishek Gilke - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for the respondent [R-1].
 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 17.03.2020 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur (M.P.) in Claim Case No.73/2018, whereby an amount of Rs.2,68,816/- has been awarded to the appellant / claimant with interest.

2 . Learned counsel for the appellant submits that since the appellant was school teacher, therefore,
he can be treated as skilled labourer.

The income of the appellant has been assessed as Rs.7500/-
which is on the lower side, whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an skilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.9185/-.

sentences.text:
He further submits that learned Claims Tribunal has also erred in not awarding any amount in the head of future prospects, whereas as per para 59.4 of National Insurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9018 2 MA-448-2021 Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 , looking to the age 51 years of the injured, 10%
amount is to be added in the head of Future Prospects.
3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that in the accident, appellant / injured has suffered grievous injuries, fracture of fibula bone of left side and large degloving wound over anterior posterior aspect of left leg.

For this, he has filed disability certificate Ex.P/116 to the extent of 40% disability which has been proved by Dr. N.K. Gupta (AW-2) and the same has not been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal, therefore, he prays that at least 15% disablement should have been given in proportion of the whole body.

His contention is that looking to the grievous injuries, learned Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding a meager amount in the head of pain and Gaytri Dikshit vs The New India Insurance Company Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123312849/
1 suffering which should be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.

sentences.text: On these contentions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

5. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9018 3 MA-448-2021 counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
From perusal of the record, it reveals that in the accident the appellant / injured has suffered grievous injuries and also fracture of fibula bone.

For this, he has filed disability certificate Ex.P/116 to the extent of 40% disability which has been proved by Dr. N.K. Gupta (AW-2) therefore, keeping in view the evidence available in this regard, this Court is of the view that at least 15% permanent disability is assessed in proportion to the whole body.

Since appellant was a school teacher,
therefore, he is treated as a skilled labourer.

Hence, as per Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, on the date of accident, income of the appellant is to be taken as Rs.9185/- considering him as 'skilled Labour' and for this judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @
Chandraram & Anr. vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

sentences.text:
Appellant /
injured was 51 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi's case (Supra), 10% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects.

Amount awarded in the head of pain and suffering is on lower side which is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
7.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.2,00,049/-
Permanent Disability:
[(Rs.9185/- + 918.5) x 12 x 11 x 15/100] Loss of income Rs.60,000/-
 Medical Expenses Rs.1,43,816/-
 Transport and attendance Rs.15,000/-
 Special Diet Rs.25,000/-
 Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
 Total: Rs.4,93,865/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9018 Gaytri Dikshit vs The New India Insurance Company Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123312849/
2  4   MACT Awarded: Rs.2,68,816/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.2,25,049/-
8.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.4,93,865/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.2,68,816/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.2,25,049/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
9. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / injured is allowed to the extent as indicated herein-above.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate which has been fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal in the impugned award.
